meta.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
meta.author: bank-team-web-development
meta.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.stem: A clerk wants an element invisible but still occupying layout space. Which property?

options.text: visibility: hidden, because it hides content while preserving space.
display: none, because it hides content and keeps space.
opacity: 0, because it removes the element from layout.
position: absolute, because it keeps space in flow.

questions.explanation: visibility hidden preserves space. display none removes it.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.stem: In a grid, when is free space calculated for fr tracks?

options.text: Before any track is sized, using the full container width.
After fixed and auto tracks are sized, the remainder becomes free space.
Only when the container has a fixed height.
Never, because fr tracks size to content.

questions.explanation: Fixed and auto tracks size first, then fr shares the remainder. The other options misstate the order.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.stem: A clerk sets min-width on a flex item but it still shrinks below it. Why?

options.text: flex-shrink always overrides min-width.
min-width never applies to flex items.
min-width alone may be overridden by flex-shrink unless flex-basis and min-width align; check the basis.
min-width only works with percentage values.

questions.explanation: min-width sets a floor, but flex-basis and shrink interactions matter. The other options deny or overstate behavior.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.stem: Explain why a box with width 100px and 10px padding is wider than 100px on screen.

answer.exemplar: With the default content-box, width covers only content, so 10px padding on each side adds 20px, making the box 120px wide.

questions.explanation: content-box adds padding outside declared width. The tempting exact-width idea ignores padding.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.stem: Which order correctly describes document to painted boxes?

options.text: Composite, then paint, then layout.
Paint first, then layout, then parse HTML.
Layout, then parse HTML, then paint.
Parse HTML, build DOM, compute styles, layout, paint, composite.

questions.explanation: The pipeline parses, builds DOM, styles, lays out, paints, composites. Reversed orders are wrong.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.stem: How is an HTML document represented in memory by the browser?

options.text: As a flat sequence of typed tokens only.
As a tree of nodes, where elements can contain other elements.
As a relational database of tags.
As a single string with no structure.

questions.explanation: The DOM is a tree of nodes. Tokens are an intermediate parsing stage, not the final structure.
questions.hint: DOM is a tree of nodes.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.stem: What happens when a div is written inside a p element?

options.text: The browser discards the div entirely.
The div nests inside the paragraph normally.
The paragraph auto-closes before the div, so the div is not a child of p.
The paragraph and div merge into one element.

questions.explanation: A block inside p auto-closes the paragraph. Nesting or discarding does not occur.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.stem: A clerk uses display none to hide a label but the layout shifts. Why?

options.text: display none only works on inline elements.
display none keeps space but hides content.
The label was absolutely positioned and cannot shift.
display none removes the element from layout, so space collapses.

questions.explanation: display none removes the element from layout. visibility hidden would preserve space.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.stem: Explain how to compute the size of a 1fr track in a 100px 1fr grid with a 300px container.

answer.exemplar: Subtract the fixed track: 300 minus 100 equals 200px free space, which the single 1fr track takes.

questions.explanation: Free space is container minus fixed tracks. The tempting full-container division ignores the fixed track.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.stem: A clerk wants a sidebar to never shrink. Which declaration?

options.text: flex-grow: 0, because grow prevents shrinking.
flex-shrink: 0, so the item keeps its basis on overflow.
flex-basis: 0, because zero basis locks size.
flex: 1, because it disables shrinking.

questions.explanation: flex-shrink 0 prevents shrinking. Grow, basis, or flex 1 do not serve this purpose.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.stem: Which box-sizing value makes width include padding and border?

options.text: padding-box, a standard value in all browsers.
content-box, because it is the initial and therefore includes all.
border-box, so the declared width covers content, padding, and border.
inherit, because it copies the inclusive behavior.

questions.explanation: border-box includes padding and border. content-box and padding-box do not.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.stem: Which stage determines the size and position of each element?

options.text: Composite, because it arranges layers.
Paint, because it draws boxes at their positions.
Parse, because it reads element sizes from HTML.
Layout, because it computes geometry from styles.

questions.explanation: Layout computes geometry. Paint draws, parse reads markup, composite layers.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.stem: A clerk thinks the browser renders directly from HTML tokens. Why wrong?

options.text: Tokens are rendered directly without any tree.
Tokens are parsed into a DOM tree first, and rendering uses the tree.
The DOM is built only after painting completes.
Tokens and DOM are identical structures.

questions.explanation: Parsing produces a DOM tree before rendering. Tokens are not the final structure.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.stem: Explain why a paragraph cannot contain a block element like a div.

answer.exemplar: HTML parsing rules auto-close a p when a block-level element starts, so the div becomes a sibling rather than a child.

questions.explanation: Block starts auto-close p. The tempting nesting idea violates parsing rules.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.stem: A clerk wants an element invisible but still interactive and in layout. Which approach?

options.text: display: none, because it keeps the element interactive.
visibility: hidden, because it keeps interactivity.
opacity: 0, because it hides visually while keeping space and interactivity.
position: fixed, because it hides visually.

questions.explanation: opacity 0 keeps space and interactivity. visibility hidden removes interactivity.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.stem: In a grid with auto 1fr, what size does auto take?

options.text: It copies the 1fr track's size.
It takes all free space, leaving nothing for 1fr.
It collapses to zero if content is small.
It sizes to its content, and 1fr takes the remaining free space.

questions.explanation: auto sizes to content; 1fr takes the rest. The other options misstate auto behavior.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.stem: How does min-width interact with flex-shrink when the line overflows?

options.text: flex-shrink ignores min-width and shrinks freely.
flex-shrink cannot reduce the item below min-width.
min-width disables flex-shrink entirely.
min-width only applies after shrinking completes.

questions.explanation: min-width floors the size during shrinking. Ignoring or disabling are wrong.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.stem: A clerk computes 100px width plus 5px border as 105px. What is missing?

options.text: Margins must be added as well.
Nothing; border alone completes the width.
Padding on both sides, if any, must also be added for content-box.
The border is already included in width by default.

questions.explanation: content-box adds padding and border. Padding must be included; margins are outside the box.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.stem: Explain what the paint stage does in the rendering pipeline.

answer.exemplar: Paint fills in pixels for text, colors, borders, and images according to the computed layout.

questions.explanation: Paint produces pixels. Layout computes geometry; composite layers them.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.stem: Which node type represents an HTML element in the DOM?

options.text: Document node, which is each individual element.
Text node, which represents tags.
Comment node, which holds element data.
Element node, which can have child nodes and attributes.

questions.explanation: Element nodes represent tags. Text, comment, and document nodes serve other purposes.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.stem:
A clerk writes

text

block

. How many top-level elements result?

options.text: One paragraph containing both text and div.
Two siblings: a paragraph containing text, then the div.
One div containing text and paragraph.
Nothing renders because the markup is invalid.

questions.explanation: The div auto-closes the p, producing two siblings. Nesting or discarding does not occur.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.stem: Does visibility: hidden remove an element from the accessibility tree?

options.text: Only if display is also none.
No, hidden content remains fully announced.
Yes, hidden content is not exposed to assistive technology.
It depends on the browser's random choice.

questions.explanation: visibility hidden hides from assistive tech. The other options misstate behavior.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.stem: A clerk sets 1fr 1fr but tracks overflow their content. Why?

options.text: Two fr tracks always overflow by design.
fr tracks never overflow content.
The container must have a fixed height to prevent overflow.
fr tracks can shrink below content minimum unless minmax sets a floor.

questions.explanation: fr tracks respect content minimums, which can overflow. A floor via minmax helps.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.stem: Explain how overflow hidden interacts with a non-shrinking flex item.

answer.exemplar: A flex-shrink 0 item keeps its size, and overflow hidden clips any content that extends beyond the container.

questions.explanation: Non-shrinking items keep size; overflow hidden clips excess. The tempting shrink idea is wrong.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.stem: A clerk wants all elements to honor their declared width including padding. What reset?

options.text: Apply box-sizing: content-box globally, the default.
Apply box-sizing: border-box globally.
Remove all padding from elements.
options.misconception: avoids padding instead of solving sizing

options.text: Use width: auto everywhere.

questions.explanation: border-box makes width include padding and border. The other options keep the surprise or avoid padding.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.stem: Which stage combines painted layers into the final screen image?

options.text: Layout, because it stacks layers.
Paint, because it merges layers.
Composite, because it merges layers for display.
Parse, because it assembles the final image.

questions.explanation: Composite merges layers. Paint produces layers; layout computes geometry; parse builds DOM.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.stem: How do you access a parent element from a child node in the DOM?

options.text: Parents are inaccessible from children.
Use childNodes to go upward.
Use nextSibling to reach the parent.
Use parentNode or parentElement property.

questions.explanation: parentNode/parentElement give the parent. Sibling and child properties do not.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.stem: A clerk nests a section inside a p and validation warns. Why?

options.text: Section elements are invalid everywhere.
Section is flow content and cannot be a child of p, so p auto-closes.
Paragraphs cannot contain any children at all.
Validation is wrong and the nesting is fine.

questions.explanation: p cannot contain flow content like section, so it auto-closes. The other options overstate or deny the rule.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.stem: Explain the difference between CSS visibility hidden and aria-hidden true.

answer.exemplar: visibility hidden hides visually and from assistive tech while preserving space; aria-hidden only affects the accessibility tree.

questions.explanation: visibility hidden affects both visual and a11y; aria-hidden affects only a11y. The tempting equivalence is wrong.
questions.hint: visibility affects both; aria-hidden a11y only.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.stem: How does gap affect free space calculation for fr tracks?

options.text: Gap disables fr sizing entirely.
Gap is added on top of fr sizing.
Gap is subtracted from free space before fr tracks share the remainder.
Gap is ignored in free space calculation.

questions.explanation: Gap reduces free space before fr distribution. The other options misstate gap handling.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.stem: A clerk has a non-shrinking item that overflows. Which property can wrap it instead?

options.text: flex-grow: 0, because it enables wrapping.
flex-shrink: 1, because it wraps overflowing items.
overflow: wrap, a valid property.
flex-wrap: wrap, so the item moves to a new line.

questions.explanation: flex-wrap wrap moves items to new lines. Shrink, grow, or invented overflow do not wrap.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.stem: Why does border-box make widths more predictable?

options.text: It removes padding and border from rendering.
Padding and border are included in the declared width, so outer size matches.
It makes width refer only to content, like content-box.
It disables margins so layouts stop shifting.

questions.explanation: border-box includes padding and border in width. Removal or content-only ideas are wrong.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.stem: A clerk thinks styles are computed before the DOM is built. Why wrong?

options.text: The DOM is built only after painting finishes.
Styles are computed during HTML parsing before any DOM node exists.
The DOM must exist first so selectors can match elements.
Styles and DOM are built simultaneously with no dependency.

questions.explanation: Selectors need DOM nodes to match, so DOM comes first. The other options reverse or deny the dependency.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.stem: Explain how querySelector traverses the DOM tree to find an element.

answer.exemplar: It performs a depth-first search of the DOM tree and returns the first element matching the selector.

questions.explanation: querySelector does a depth-first search and returns the first match. The tempting all-matches idea is querySelectorAll.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.stem: A clerk needs a paragraph with an emphasized phrase. What is valid?

options.text: Use p containing a ul, because lists are inline.
Use p containing a div, because div is inline by default.
Use p containing a section, because section is phrasing content.
Use p with inline span or em, because inline children are allowed in p.

questions.explanation: p allows phrasing content like span and em. div, section, and ul are flow content and auto-close p.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.stem: Which technique hides content visually while keeping it in layout and screen readers?

options.text: display: none, because it keeps space and a11y.
A visually hidden CSS pattern, such as clip and absolute positioning off-screen.
visibility: hidden, because it keeps a11y announcement.
opacity: 0 alone, because it is always accessible.

questions.explanation: Visually hidden patterns hide visually but remain accessible. display none and visibility hidden remove a11y.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.stem: What does repeat(3, 1fr) create in a grid container?

options.text: Three fixed 1px tracks.
One track repeated three times as a single 3fr track.
Three equal fractional tracks sharing free space.
An invalid declaration that browsers ignore.

questions.explanation: repeat(3, 1fr) creates three equal tracks. Single-track or invalid readings are wrong.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.stem: A clerk sets min-width auto on a flex item and it refuses to shrink. Why?

options.text: It forces the item to grow instead.
auto min-width disables flex-shrink entirely.
auto is invalid for min-width in flex.
min-width auto resolves to the content size, preventing shrink below content.

questions.explanation: min-width auto resolves to content size, flooring shrink. The other options overstate or misstate behavior.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.stem: Explain how calc can help a clerk account for padding in a width.

answer.exemplar: Use calc(100% - 40px) to subtract padding from the container width when content-box is in effect.

questions.explanation: calc subtracts padding from container width under content-box. border-box is simpler but calc works too.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.stem: Which stage turns HTML text into a DOM tree?

options.text: Layout, because it reads HTML into boxes.
Parse, because it tokenizes and builds the DOM.
Paint, because it creates nodes from markup.
Composite, because it assembles the tree.

questions.explanation: Parse builds the DOM. Layout, paint, and composite occur later.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.stem: What happens to the DOM when JavaScript appends a new element?

options.text: Nothing changes until the page reloads.
The HTML source file is rewritten on disk.
A new node is inserted into the tree, and the render pipeline updates.
The browser rebuilds the entire document from scratch.

questions.explanation: DOM mutation inserts a node and triggers render updates. Source files and full rebuilds are not involved.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.stem: Which element is valid as a child of a paragraph?

options.text: ul, because lists are phrasing content.
div, because it can be inline.
section, because it is phrasing content.
em, because it is phrasing content.

questions.explanation: em is phrasing content and valid in p. div, section, and ul are flow content and auto-close p.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.stem: A clerk sets aria-hidden true on a visible element. What happens?

options.text: It becomes invisible on screen and in assistive tech.
Assistive technology ignores it, but it remains visible on screen.
It is removed from the DOM entirely.
Nothing happens because aria-hidden is invalid.

questions.explanation: aria-hidden affects only the accessibility tree. The visual rendering stays.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.stem: Explain how minmax(0, 1fr) differs from 1fr alone.

answer.exemplar: minmax(0, 1fr) allows the track to shrink to zero, while plain 1fr respects content minimums.

questions.explanation: minmax(0, 1fr) sets a zero floor, allowing shrink below content minimums. Plain 1fr does not.
questions.hint: Zero floor allows shrink to zero.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.stem: A clerk wants a fixed 200px item that never shrinks. Which declaration?

options.text: flex: 0 1 200px, because shrink 1 locks size.
flex: 1 0 200px, because grow 1 still prevents shrink.
flex: 0 0 200px, so grow 0, shrink 0, basis 200px.
flex: 200px, because a single value locks grow and shrink.

questions.explanation: flex: 0 0 200px sets grow 0, shrink 0, basis 200px. The other shorthands allow shrink or grow.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.stem: Which box model value includes margins in the measured size?

options.text: padding-box includes margins and padding.
border-box includes margins along with padding and border.
content-box includes margins in the content width.
None of the standard box-sizing values include margins; margins are always outside.

questions.explanation: No box-sizing value includes margins; they are always outside the box. The other options overstate inclusion.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.stem: What can block rendering of a page?

options.text: Images always block rendering completely.
Synchronous scripts and stylesheets in the head can block rendering.
Nothing can block rendering in modern browsers.
Only HTML comments block rendering.

questions.explanation: Synchronous head resources can block rendering. Images and comments do not block in that way.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.stem: A clerk assumes shadow DOM nodes appear in document.querySelectorAll. Why wrong?

options.text: querySelectorAll cannot run on documents with shadow DOM.
Shadow DOM nodes are always visible to document queries.
Shadow DOM is encapsulated and not part of the light DOM queried by document.
Shadow DOM replaces the entire document tree.

questions.explanation: Shadow DOM is encapsulated and excluded from document queries. The other options misstate behavior.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.stem: Explain why a paragraph can contain a span but not a div.

answer.exemplar: Paragraphs allow phrasing content like span, while div is flow content and auto-closes the paragraph.

questions.explanation: p allows phrasing content; flow content auto-closes p. The tempting nesting idea is wrong.
questions.hint: span is phrasing; div is flow.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.stem: A clerk wants an element's children to participate in parent layout while the element itself disappears. Which value?

options.text: opacity: 0, because it removes the box.
display: none, because it keeps children in layout.
visibility: hidden, because it removes the box but keeps children.
display: contents, because it removes the box but keeps children.

questions.explanation: display contents removes the element's box but keeps children. The other values do not.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.stem: What does grid-auto-flow: dense do?

options.text: It makes all tracks the same size.
It fills holes in the grid by placing smaller items in gaps.
It disables fractional tracks.
It sorts items alphabetically.

questions.explanation: dense fills holes with smaller items. The other options misstate its effect.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.stem: How can a clerk allow a flex item to shrink below its content size?

options.text: Set flex-shrink: 0, which enables shrinking.
Set min-width: auto, which allows full shrink.
Set min-width: 0, overriding the content-based minimum.
Set overflow: visible, which reduces minimum size.

questions.explanation: min-width 0 overrides the content minimum and allows shrink. auto, shrink 0, or overflow do not.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.stem: A clerk sets width 100% and padding 20px with content-box and gets horizontal scroll. Why?

options.text: Scroll appears because margins collapse.
Percentage widths ignore padding automatically.
The browser rounds 100% up, causing scroll.
Padding adds to the 100% width, causing overflow.

questions.explanation: content-box adds padding to 100%, overflowing. The other options misstate behavior.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.stem: Explain what will-change hints to the browser.

answer.exemplar: will-change hints which properties will animate, allowing the browser to optimize layers ahead of time.

questions.explanation: will-change hints upcoming changes for optimization. The tempting no-effect idea is wrong.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.stem: A clerk wants to remove an element from the DOM. Which method?

options.text: element.delete(), a standard DOM method.
element.remove(), which removes the node from its parent.
element.hide(), which removes from the DOM.
document.delete(element), the standard removal API.

questions.explanation: element.remove() removes the node. delete, hide, and document.delete are not standard removal methods.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.stem: Which markup keeps a paragraph as a single element with emphasized text?

options.text:
Hello

world
, splitting into two elements.

Hello

world

, nesting block in p.

Hello world

, using inline em inside p.

Hello world

, wrapping p in div.

questions.explanation: Inline em inside p keeps one paragraph. Block nesting auto-closes p.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.stem: Does opacity: 0 remove an element from the accessibility tree?

options.text: It depends on the browser's random choice.
Yes, opacity 0 hides from assistive tech.
Only if combined with pointer-events none.
No, opacity 0 content remains accessible to screen readers.

questions.explanation: opacity 0 keeps a11y. The other options misstate behavior.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.stem: A clerk sets 1fr 1fr with a 10px gap in a 100px container. What is each track?

options.text: 50px each, because gap is ignored in fr sizing.
45px each, because 10px gap leaves 90px split equally.
40px each, because gap is subtracted twice.
100px each, because fr ignores container width.

questions.explanation: Gap reduces free space: 100 - 10 = 90, split equally gives 45. The other options misstate gap handling.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.stem: Explain why a flex-shrink 0 item can cause overflow instead of shrinking.

answer.exemplar: flex-shrink 0 locks the item's size, so on overflow the item stays fixed and other items or the container must absorb the excess.

questions.explanation: Shrink 0 locks size, forcing overflow or other items to absorb. The tempting shrink-anyway idea is wrong.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.stem: What is the root cause of the box-sizing surprise?

options.text: Margins are included in width by default.
The default border-box includes too much in width.
The default content-box excludes padding and border from width.
Padding is automatically zero for all elements.

questions.explanation: content-box excludes padding and border from width, causing surprise. The other options misstate defaults.
